pack.description: Vocabulary of technology passages and talks: computing, engineering, innovation and its effects.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory technology texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: a set of exact steps that a computer follows to solve a problem or complete a task
entries.example_academic: The algorithm ranks results according to how often other pages link to them.
entries.example_spoken: The algorithm keeps showing me the same videos.

entries.definition: the use of machines and computers to do work that people used to do
entries.example_academic: Automation has eliminated routine tasks while raising demand for technical skills.
entries.example_spoken: Automation at the warehouse means fewer night shifts.

entries.definition: the amount of data that a connection can carry in a given time
entries.example_academic: Video conferencing requires far more bandwidth than email.
entries.example_spoken: There's not enough bandwidth in the dorm when everyone streams.

entries.definition: the process of changing information into a secret code so that only certain people can read it
entries.example_academic: Strong encryption protects messages even if they are intercepted.
entries.example_spoken: The app uses encryption, so the company can't read your chats.

entries.definition: the way a person and a computer program communicate, such as the screens and menus the person sees
entries.example_academic: A simple interface reduces the time new users need to learn the system.
entries.example_spoken: The new interface is cleaner, but I can't find anything.

entries.definition: the first working model of a machine or product, made to test the design
entries.example_academic: The prototype failed at high temperatures and had to be redesigned.
entries.example_spoken: We have to demo our prototype on Friday.

entries.definition: no longer used because something newer and better exists
entries.example_academic: Printed timetables became obsolete once passengers could check their phones.
entries.example_spoken: My laptop is basically obsolete; it can't run the software.

entries.definition: computer systems that can do tasks which normally need human thinking, such as understanding language
entries.example_academic: Artificial intelligence now assists doctors in reading medical images.
entries.example_spoken: Our professor lets us use artificial intelligence to check grammar, but not to write.

entries.definition: a large, organized collection of information stored on a computer
entries.example_academic: The database links each patient's records across different hospitals.
entries.example_spoken: You can search the library database from home.

entries.definition: a device that detects heat, light, movement or another signal and reacts to it
entries.example_academic: Sensors embedded in the bridge report tiny changes in vibration.
entries.example_spoken: The lights have a motion sensor, so they turn off by themselves.

entries.definition: a computer model that copies a real situation so that it can be studied or practiced
entries.example_academic: The simulation predicted how smoke would spread through the building.
entries.example_spoken: We ran the simulation a hundred times and got the same result.

entries.definition: a material, such as silicon, that carries electricity in a limited way and is used to make computer chips
entries.example_academic: Advances in semiconductor design doubled processing power every few years.
entries.example_spoken: There's a shortage of semiconductors, so laptops cost more.

entries.definition: the protection of computers, networks and data against attack or theft
entries.example_academic: Cybersecurity has become a board-level concern for most large firms.
entries.example_spoken: She's taking a cybersecurity course next semester.

entries.definition: able to work together with another device or program, or able to exist together
entries.example_academic: The new standard is compatible with equipment installed a decade ago.
entries.example_spoken: Is this charger compatible with your phone?

entries.definition: an important discovery or development that solves a problem
entries.example_academic: The breakthrough came when the team abandoned the original design.
entries.example_spoken: We finally had a breakthrough with the code last night.

entries.definition: an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell an invention for a number of years
entries.example_academic: The firm filed a patent to protect the manufacturing process.
entries.example_spoken: He holds a patent for a folding bike lock.

entries.definition: able to be made larger or to handle more work without serious problems
entries.example_academic: A scalable architecture lets the service absorb sudden increases in traffic.
entries.example_spoken: The idea works for ten users, but is it scalable?

entries.definition: the delay between sending a signal or request and getting the response
entries.example_academic: Low latency is essential for remote surgery and online gaming.
entries.example_spoken: There's too much latency on this call; we keep talking over each other.

entries.definition: the inclusion of extra parts or copies so that a system keeps working if one part fails; also, the state of not being needed
entries.example_academic: Redundancy in the power supply prevented an outage when one generator failed.
entries.example_spoken: Keep a backup on another drive; you need some redundancy.

entries.definition: the ability of different computer systems or programs to exchange and use each other's information
entries.example_academic: Interoperability between hospital systems would reduce duplicated tests.
entries.example_spoken: Without interoperability, we'd have to retype everything.

entries.definition: owned and controlled by one company, so that others cannot freely use or copy it
entries.example_academic: The file was saved in a proprietary format that other programs could not open.
entries.example_spoken: It's proprietary software, so you can't see the code.

entries.definition: describing software whose code anyone may read, change and share
entries.example_academic: Open source projects rely on volunteers to find and repair security flaws.
entries.example_spoken: We used an open source tool, so it didn't cost anything.

entries.definition: changing an industry or way of doing things completely; also, causing trouble that interrupts an activity
entries.example_academic: Disruptive technologies often begin by serving customers that established firms ignore.
entries.example_spoken: His phone kept ringing, which was really disruptive.

entries.definition: the state of becoming old-fashioned and no longer useful
entries.example_academic: Planned obsolescence shortens the life of products in order to stimulate sales.
entries.example_spoken: Phones are designed for obsolescence after about three years.

entries.definition: the science of making and using extremely small structures, the size of a few atoms
entries.example_academic: Nanotechnology has produced coatings that repel water and resist bacteria.
entries.example_spoken: He works on nanotechnology for drug delivery.

entries.definition: a method in which computer programs improve at a task by finding patterns in large amounts of data instead of following fixed rules
entries.example_academic: Machine learning models are only as reliable as the data on which they were trained.
entries.example_spoken: The spam filter uses machine learning to get better over time.

entries.definition: to repeat a process several times, improving the result each time
entries.example_academic: Designers iterate rapidly, testing each version with a small group of users.
entries.example_spoken: We iterated on the design until the professor was happy.

entries.definition: the amount of work, data or material that a system processes in a given time
entries.example_academic: The upgrade doubled the throughput of the assembly line.
entries.example_spoken: The lab's throughput went up when they bought a second machine.

entries.definition: seeming to be everywhere
entries.example_academic: Ubiquitous connectivity has blurred the boundary between work and leisure.
entries.example_spoken: Those electric scooters are ubiquitous downtown.
